If I could give zero stars, I would.

My partner recently won a boudoir experience and the way she was spoken to on the phone was absolutely unacceptable.

What was advertised as a “prize” quickly turned into what felt like a financial screening. It became very clear during the call that unless she was prepared to spend over £1,000, she was not the kind of winner they were interested in. That expectation was never stated anywhere in the advertising.

If you are not prepared to break the bank, do not apply.

The £250 credit is presented as part of the prize, but it became obvious that it holds very little value unless you are committing to a much larger spend. That lack of transparency is deeply disappointing.

The tone noticeably shifted the moment she mentioned she was a student. The conversation became dismissive and condescending. Instead of feeling excited about something she had won, she was made to feel judged and spoken down to because of her financial situation.

Boudoir photography is meant to be empowering and confidence-building. Speaking to someone in a way that makes them feel small completely contradicts that purpose. If this experience is only intended for high-spending clients, that should be made clear from the outset.

I ordered £90.24 of goods in April 2026. The order was marked as delivered by the courier but never arrived. I contacted The Skinny Food Co the same day and made several follow-up phone calls in the days that followed. It took 7 days to receive a first response.

When they did respond, I was asked to complete a courier claim form and was told that resolution would be dependent on the outcome of the courier's investigation. This is not consistent with UK consumer law, under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, the retailer is responsible for delivery, not the courier. I flagged this in writing at the time.

After their own investigation deadline passed with no update or resolution, a replacement order was eventually sent after I chased them. That also failed to arrive. At this point I formally requested a refund. The response I received was a holding email and a 10% discount code.

Nearly two months on from the original order, having dealt with two lost deliveries, repeated unmet deadlines, and having had to send numerous emails asserting my legal rights just to receive basic responses, I have received no refund and have been left with no option but to initiate a chargeback through my credit card provider and report the matter to Trading Standards.

The products may well be fine, I wouldn't know, I never received them. But the customer service has been consistently poor throughout, and the attempt to shift legal responsibility onto their courier is something other customers should be aware of. I will not be ordering from this company again.

EDIT: I see a lot of other similar negative reviews. To all those people, please report to Trading Standards via Citizens Advice (citizensadvice.org.uk/consumer/get-more-help/report-to-trading-standards).

The waiting room was overcrowded, Harley was extremely stressed, and her tail was actively bleeding while we waited. Despite this, she wasn’t even booked in until after 9am. No apology. No communication.

I then had to chase THEM for updates. At 3pm I rang and was told she hadn’t even gone into surgery yet. At 6pm I rang again, only to be told she’d already been done, recovered, and was ready to collect. No one had even bothered to inform me. When I questioned it, I was told “I don’t know.”

Aftercare instructions said her bandage must stay on until a post-op appointment on Saturday. When I tried to book it, I was told there were no appointments and had to accept Sunday instead. So already, the aftercare plan they gave me wasn’t even achievable.

That same night, her bandage came off. I rang them and was told I’d have to pay £99 emergency fee PLUS £26 just to rebandage it — for something that clearly wasn’t done properly in the first place. When I took her in, I was then told she didn’t even need a bandage… despite being told the complete opposite just hours before.

The next night, she lost stitches and there was blood everywhere. I rushed her back, and within minutes they had stapled her tail and rebandaged it — with NO anaesthetic. No numbing. Nothing. Just stapled a fresh surgical wound. I’m still in disbelief writing that.

By Saturday morning, the bandage had come off AGAIN. Harley was crying, clearly in pain, and couldn’t sit or lie down comfortably even with pain relief. I rang for help and was told a nurse would call me back. Two hours later, nothing. When I rang again, the nurse was rude and dismissive, saying “I was going to call you” and that callbacks happen “later in the day” — despite me being told otherwise.

She then told me AGAIN that Harley didn’t need a bandage and said I could “bring her in this afternoon” but couldn’t give me a time — just expected me to sit and wait indefinitely with an anxious, post-op dog who’s meant to be on strict rest.

The lack of care, consistency, communication and basic compassion has been absolutely disgusting. At every stage, I’ve been given conflicting advice, no support, and made to feel like an inconvenience rather than someone trying to care for their dog.

This isn’t just poor service — this is a serious concern for animal welfare. Under the Animal Welfare Act 2006, animals should be protected from unnecessary suffering. From what I’ve experienced, that standard has not been met.

Vets are supposed to care. They’re supposed to reassure you, guide you, and most importantly, look after your pet. Instead, this felt rushed, disorganised, money-driven, and completely lacking in compassion.

Please, if you’re local and considering where to take your pet, do your research. I wouldn’t wish this experience on anyone or any animal.

Harley deserved better than this.

LSS London feels less like a serious security service and more like a box-ticking exercise designed to extract easy money. I live in a genuinely safe area, yet this company presents itself as if it’s providing some essential layer of protection. In reality, the “service” amounts to little more than a single car occasionally driving around—hardly a reassuring or effective security presence.

For something marketed as neighbourhood security, the effort appears minimal and borderline performative. There’s no visible sense of vigilance, no meaningful engagement, and certainly nothing that justifies the cost. It raises the question of what, exactly, residents are paying for.

What’s even more concerning is the apparent lack of proper training. Requiring just a two-day course to work for the company does not inspire confidence in their ability to handle real security situations. Keeping a neighbourhood safe requires skill, awareness, and preparation—not a rushed introduction that barely scratches the surface.

Overall, it feels like a service built on perception rather than substance. For the price being charged, the value simply isn’t there.

At a recent farmers show I attended I purchased two pies from the stall, one large Wild Beaver pie and a pork pie. The display looked fantastic, showcasing the pie fillings. I was impressed by the meat content  and so on that basis I decide I would get some.
Well the wild Beaver pie which I cooked that evening was nothing short of truly disappointing. Prior to cooking the pie I had noticed it had collapsed on one side. Once cooked I cut into it, expecting it to hold its shape. Well as soon as I did it sunk, I severed each portion, I’d cut it into 4. I had one small chunk of meat in my quarter, my husband had 4 chunks, my two sons had 3-4 small chunks. To give you an idea the chunks were the size of an OXO cube . I was disgusted that the pie had shown it was packed full on the display at the show. The taste wasn’t any better, the gravy was thin, no richness to it as I’d expect and I couldn’t taste any ale. We all thought it was terrible. The only one positive thing I could say about it was that the pastry was nice, but I didn’t pay £11.50 for that. The pork pie was next, surly this was going to be the star. Unfortunately not, the meat quality was very poor and it had a very cheep sausage meat flavour. Like a tin of spam. Cat food pie my husband called it. I am a foodie and I make my own pies, quite how this company exists producing this stuff is beyond me, I would expect this standard from a budget supermarket brand not a company like this.

We will not be buying again

Purchased a car from Hilton Garage and within 31 days of ownership the sunroof mechanism completely failed and became stuck open. The car was left exposed to water ingress and could not be safely or properly used.

I took the vehicle to an authorised Kia dealership for diagnosis, where I was informed there was evidence of prior tampering with the sunroof mechanism. I was advised the repair would require an expensive motor that is currently on back order with no estimated delivery date, and that the repair may not even be covered under the premium warranty I was sold with the vehicle because of the evidence of tampering.

Despite paying extra for a 3-year premium warranty for peace of mind, I have effectively been left to deal with the issue entirely on my own. The warranty company has not accepted the claim, leaving me with significant repair costs and no meaningful support.

I contacted Hilton Garage multiple times by email, including a formal rejection notice and follow-up correspondence, but received no acknowledgement or response whatsoever. Being completely ignored after spending a substantial amount of money on a vehicle has been extremely disappointing and stressful.

Because I still needed transport for work, I was forced to spend even more money attempting to secure and repair the sunroof through an RAC-approved garage. I sourced multiple replacement motors myself from eBay, none of which worked once installed, and I still had to pay labour costs despite the issue remaining unresolved. The parts also cannot now be returned because they had to be assembled into the car during testing.

Overall, this has been an extremely frustrating and costly experience. I expected much better customer service, support, and accountability after purchasing a vehicle and extended warranty through a dealership.

I will now be taking this matter further through the appropriate legal and consumer protection channels due to the complete lack of response and accountability shown throughout this situation.

Please avoid this place for your health and safety!

one_star_reviews.text:
I had every intention of resolving this matter privately and without the need for public comment. However, after repeated attempts to obtain a reasonable and professional resolution from both ChipsAway.International (the franchisor) and ChipsAway Nottingham (the franchisee) have been ignored, I believe it is important to set out the facts clearly for the benefit of other potential customers.

I initially instructed ChipsAway Nottingham to carry out a minor cosmetic repair to my vehicle, valued at £70,000. Following that work, I also requested a full polish of the car, Upon completion , I immediately identified significant blotching, hazing, and visible defects across the paintwork which were not present prior to their involvement.
The damage became increasingly visible when the car was wet.

When I raised these concerns, I received written correspondence from ChipsAway Nottingham which was, frankly, astonishing. They expressly admitted that the incorrect sealant had been used, that he knew the product was unsuitable for the vehicle, that he was aware it was likely to cause damage, and that he could actually see the damage occurring during application. He further confirmed that, due to the hot weather conditions at the time, the sealant should not have been applied at all.

Despite these clear admissions, ChipsAway.Nottingham attempted to minimise the issue by describing it as “an easy fix” which simply required polishing off. Acting in good faith, and relying on those assurances, I permitted a second remedial attempt to be carried out.

Following this, the vehicle was stored in a garage over winter. When it was brought back into use in late March, the identical defects reappeared in precisely the same locations. These markings have been fully photographed and documented and directly correspond with the original damage for which responsibility had already effectively been accepted.

Since that point, the conduct of both the franchisor and franchisee has been wholly unacceptable. Rather than dealing with the issue responsibly, ChipsAway International attempted to distance itself by placing responsibility solely on the franchisee, while ChipsAway Nottingham has become evasive and increasingly unprofessional.
They have stated that they hold zero responsibility and all services provided are not guaranteed by them and that all technicians are self employed.

Most concerning of all has been the refusal to provide details of their public liability insurance.
Even with pending court case they still will not provide any insurance details.
This is a straightforward and entirely reasonable request where damage has been caused to a customer’s vehicle and liability has effectively been acknowledged in writing. Despite repeated formal requests, ChipsAway Nottingham has refused to disclose these details, preventing the matter from being resolved through the proper insurance channels and forcing unnecessary escalation. This refusal has significantly prolonged the dispute and demonstrates a complete lack of transparency and accountability.

Had they simply acted responsibly, provided the relevant insurance information, and engaged constructively, this matter could have been resolved quickly and professionally. Instead, I have been left with no alternative but to pursue both the franchisor and franchisee through formal legal proceedings for the damage caused to my vehicle.

For the avoidance of doubt, every statement made in this review is supported by written admissions, email correspondence, and photographic evidence. Should either party seek to dispute the accuracy of this review, I will have no hesitation in relying on that evidence.

Court proceedings are now underway.

I would strongly advise any prospective customer to exercise extreme caution before entrusting this business with their vehicle.

WORST renting experience of my life, avoid using this company at all costs.

Originally rented an apartment 3 months ago for £1000 a month, so not a cheap apartment, at my viewing appointment I was left in the rain and cold outside for 50 minutes after my viewing time with no updates unless I rang for them.

When I finally got into the apartment there had been a leak in the hallway leading to the apartment, causing mould and damage to the carpets and walls, I was told this was due to be replaced and fixed imminently. I was also informed the apartment came with an ‘allocated’ parking space but the letting agent couldn’t tell me which one it was in order for me to view that as well. I was also told all CCTV worked in the car garage.

When we entered the apartment, none of the electrics or water were switched on so I couldn’t test any appliances, the letting agent promised me that all appliances worked but due to the disrepair of the kitchen cupboards it was due to have a new kitchen fitted upon a tenant taking the property, along with new carpets. I liked the size and location of the apartment and the promises made so I paid what I needed to and then arranged to move into the property. The move in date was pushed back twice due to the works being carried out but I let them off as I wanted the works to be carried out before I moved in as I was moving from another city without any support system in Nottingham and needed to move completely once I did move.

When I finally got the keys, the agent that handed them over also couldn’t tell me which car park space to use or how to enter the car park and that the reception team at the building would inform me.

When I arrived to move in, the reception informed me that it actually wasn’t allocated parking and I’d need to apply to even enter the car park, at which point it’s a free for all, with no cameras working!

Then to make things better, I’ve gone up to the apartment to find that there is no running water in the property at all, and on top of this, the only appliance in the kitchen that actually works is the washing machine. Meaning I’d just moved into an apartment in a new city with no water, no toilet, no shower, no fridge, no freezer and no oven. The hallways had also not been addressed so there was mould growing across the carpets and up the walls outside my front door.

My water was fixed after nearly a week and I’m still yet to receive a response regarding the rent I was charged for an inhabitable apartment, during this time I had to shower at local swimming baths and use restaurant toilets to survive and any time I ask for a refund in rent for this time I’m completely ignored.

It’s now been 3 months since I moved in, I’ve paid over £3000 in rent and deposits, and I still have no working kitchen. I’ve been offered a ‘temporary’ fridge whilst the landlord decides what to do next because any quote he receives is too high to take action with, I’ve declined the temporary fridge due to space restrictions and the fact that it will then delay the rest of the kitchen further, on top of this what use is a fridge without a working oven?

I’m now in the process of looking at legal options as I’ve come to the end of my wits with it all, I’m paying to eat in restaurants or with take away every single day, I can’t cook anything, I can’t live properly, the company has caused me a huge emotional and financial distress and honestly couldn’t care less about it, it’s disgusting.

Avoid avoid avoid, as I will be with paying any further rent until my problems are resolved!

During the MOT, a salesman named Luke contacted us to ask whether we wanted a valuation on the vehicle. As we were not personally on site, he explained that he would collect service book from the car himself and inspect the service history in order to complete the valuation.

The valuation was apparently completed successfully. Remarkably, however, when we got home later that day, the service book/log book had vanished into thin air.

despite previously being the person supposedly checking the vehicle history for valuation purposes.

giving the strong impression that protecting colleagues who are incompetent  arnt we luke .... mattered more than resolving a legitimate customer complaint professionally.

I ordered timber from B&Q as an essential component of a polytunnel build. From the outset, the experience was poor — it took a week just to receive a delivery date, which fell on a Sunday during a bank holiday weekend. When I requested an alternative, the next available slot was the following Sunday, as apparently they only deliver on Sundays.
The Friday before the rescheduled delivery — after my partner and I had already booked Monday and Tuesday off work to assemble the tunnel — B&Q sent me an email notification of a partial refund. No explanation. No warning. When I checked against my plans, I discovered they had silently reduced the quantity of timber in my order. The specific lengths I'd ordered for the frame had been cut, meaning the polytunnel could not be built.
Had I not investigated the partial refund myself, B&Q would have turned up on Sunday, dumped over £100 worth of timber outside my house, and left me with materials that were completely insufficient to complete the project. Meanwhile, plants that depend on the polytunnel for protection are now at risk of dying.
I called customer service. They offered nothing — no solution, no alternative, no urgency. When I demanded compensation for the wasted time off work, I was told they couldn't even look at a compensation claim until the refund had been processed, which wouldn't be until the end of the following week.
I have spent significant money at B&Q on this project. This is the worst customer experience I have ever had with any retailer — not just inconvenient but actively costly. I've cancelled the order and I will never shop at B&Q again.

I want to emphasise that this is based on Halfords policy, rather than the technician:
My battery had needed to be restarted by a breakdown mechanic. I went to the Halfords store for a battery check afterwards. They wouldn't test the health of my battery because a cover needed to be removed, which would "take 10 minutes", so I left the store. I ended up having a Halfords mobile mechanic out 2 days later (when my battery failed completely) to replace the battery and they said it was a 1 minute job to remove the cover, which it was.
It was likely I needed a battery replacement when visiting the store, so the time to take the cover off wouldn't have been "wasted" since I would have then paid for the inevitable battery replacement.

I would suggest charging a small fee (£5-10) for a battery health check, which then allows ALL batteries to be checked - after all, most batteries have some sort of cover. I would pay that fee, as most people would, for the peace of mind that the battery has been tested.
I think people should be paid for their time, so that you actually get a service. Enticing people in with a free check, on the gamble that some will need a new battery and that covers the checks that don't require a new battery is a poor overall service.

I’m not one to write bad reviews but feel that the cladding we purchased and installed from Envirobuild is so bad and has not lived up to any of the promises made on the website it is necessary to in this case. Having to give even one star feels wrong!

We purchased over £1500 worth of cladding last year in 2025 to cover an outside wall running to the side of a stone stairwell at the front of our house. Our landscaper installed the cladding using composite 50mm battens. It looked great for a few weeks but we started noticing it staining and did find it difficult to clean.

Now, just 12 months after installation and after one Cornish winter the problems have become much worse and we are now looking to strip it all out and will have to start again with a different material. It looks horrendous.

The cladding boards have warped, cracked and stained so badly it is difficult to comprehend after such a short space of time.

I need to measure this against the promises made on the website, which are:

"it’s designed to withstand rain, humidity, and moisture” - It has not withstood any of these.

"without rotting, warping, or splitting” - it has warped and split.

"Performs Well in Wet Conditions” - it has not. My 20 year old wooden shed is in better condition.

"Composite cladding typically lasts 25 to 30 years” - It has not lasted one year.

"Cleaning composite cladding is simple” & “best stain resistance" - it is not. I have followed the guidance to try and remove the staining several times but it will not come off. It looks terrible after 12 months in place.

"Comprehensive warranty – Warranties of up to 25 years covering structural integrity and fade and stain protection.” - so how good is the warranty?

I reported the issue with them and they stated that they can’t help and the warranty is void because our landscaper did not leave a 20mm gap at the top of the boards as per the installation guide. This implies that the issue is begin caused by a downward pressure but the boards are not pushing at the ends and the gap that was left is still clear of the adjacent material. They are swelling widthways where they lock together causing the boards to warp and split all the way along the wall. We have over a 50mm gap between the floor and the cladding where the problem is most severe.

They also said the warranty was void because we didn’t install a waterproof membrane. As the cladding is not on a wall to the house we deemed it unnecessary as the installation guide says the “membrane should be installed to protect the walls”, not the cladding. The cladding surely is meant to be weather resistant.

Other materials we installed in the garden project still all look like new. This includes Millboard decking and Cedar cladding which have resisted the weather incredibly well and are easy to clean. We really did trust that this cladding would be weather resistant and provide some longevity. It’s been a complete waste of money and the promises and warranty mean nothing.

Interestingly, we left the offcuts from our project outside and the few boards of cladding we have left are completely stained, warped and cracking while the Millboard leftovers are spotless and resistant to the weather. This is quite telling.

I have uploaded a filmed review of the cladding problems so you can find this by searching YouTube for “Envirobuild Cladding Nightmare”.

If you are considering buying this cladding please save yourself the time and money and choose a different, more suitable product. We’ve learnt the hard way and wasted a lot of money installing this. Avoid!

I paid up front for a year at Castle Marina.  I feel ripped off.

The residents are decent people who do a lot to support each other.  Best neighbours I ever had.

But the marina itself was awful.  Massive gulf between Aquavista's glossy marketing and what it delivered.  While recent investment may fix some issues it's still run by the same people with the same culture.

- Cold showers for weeks, even when it was -7 outside.  People complained - the marina blamed its customers for showering too much.  Possibly the first time in the 250-year history of canals that boaters were accused of being too clean.
- Inadequate domestic washers that often stop mid-cycle until you go beg the office for an extra token.  Manager declined to fix this as they'd subcontracted it to a third party (er no, that doesn't prevent responsibility to ensure your advertised service is supplied)
- Boats rushed onto an unfinished new pontoon.  No water supply on it for 5+ days, a floor panel left up and worryingly little safety gear.
- ...and trapped on it for days because the manager thought submerged debris had been discovered (didn't they check first?!?).  If someone fell off a boat onto debris or punctured their hull on it, that could have been lethal.
- AV's area manager had the nerve to tell me this was for our *benefit*.  I assure you, the people whose boats were trapped on a pontoon with no running water didn't feel like it.
- Moorers told to attend the office in person on Dec 23rd to collect letters - under the gaze of the manager - detailing for many a huge fee increase.  Demeaning, insensitive and it must have ruined a few Christamases.
- Many narrowboats forced to moor on wobbly fingers designed for river cruisers half their length.  I regularly dangled over open water to fill my water tank.  Aquavista coned them off to leave only a few feet usable but wouldn't say why in writing.  Moorings are charged by the foot of boat so does this mean I get a 75% refund? (not holding my breath...)
- Bit by bit the old pontoons got condemned as unsafe. Boats squeezed into the remaining, cramped spaces.
- Awful security.  Motorbike theft, both successful and attempted.  Parcel theft.  CCTV broken for much of the time.  Gate code leaks to non-moorers.
- Vehicle gate closes 20s after a vehicle goes through so anyone can tailgate in.  At one point a masked gang (!!) did this and had to be chased away.  The manager acknowledged the danger to customers but six months on it's still easy to do.
- Epidemic of crime on the canal.  Google "BBC Nottingham canal crime".  A bunch of dodgy boats moored near the marina for the summer - their inhabitants drinking, taking drugs and blasting out loud music.
- Marina office (where you go to have complaints ignored or learn about a massive price rise) was often closed during the advertised open hours.
- My 12-month contract said I wouldn't need to give notice if I left at the end.  Staff repeatedly pressured me to.  Area Manager confirmed no notice was required, but tried to justify it by saying they wanted to "plan berth availability" (I think this means "make more money by reselling it immediately")
- If you sell your boat while it's in the marina, Aquavista's contract gives them the right to 7.5% + VAT of its value - even if you didn't use their brokerage service.  Incredible.
- The marketing makes a lot of all the "Freedom!" you'll get if you base your boat here.  With a 3-month notice period unless I left bang on the 12-month mark and that greedy sale-on-berth charge?  Pull the other one.

It's not great for boating either.  The tight concrete entrance bend is hard for novices to get a narrowboat round without scraping it.  I asked the manager if they could at least fit a bumper - she didn't even reply to the email.  And the Nottingham canal is only five miles long: to get anywhere else you're on the big bad Trent, daunting at the best of times and can close for months when in flood.

Absolutely terrible experience with Blinds 2 Go.

We have now received FIVE separate orders/remakes and every single one has been incorrect. The original blind itself was faulty due to a defective, poor-quality tilt control and despite repeatedly explaining the issue, sending photos, measurements, order numbers, and clear descriptions, the problem still has not been resolved 2 months later.

A replacement was sent under the SureSize Guarantee, yet even the remake arrived missing the exact part that was faulty in the first place. We have now also received another completely incorrect part that is not even remotely similar to what we actually need.

Customer service has been incredibly frustrating and unhelpful throughout. They say they’re sorry but continue to carelessly send replacements that aren’t correct to look helpful. We continue to receive repetitive generic responses asking for information that has already been provided multiple times, with little evidence that anyone is properly reviewing the case and generic sorry emails

After months of delays, incorrect deliveries, poor communication, and poor product quality, we have completely lost confidence in this company. We are now escalating the matter formally and pursuing a complaint through the Ombudsman.

I would strongly advise others to think carefully before ordering from Blinds 2 Go based on our experience.

The company promised delivery within 5 working days, but the first blind only arrived after 1 month. The blinds also arrived separately over different weeks, which was extremely frustrating and inconvenient.

I called several times asking for a refund and to cancel the order, but I was always told that cancellation was impossible because the blinds were already “in production”. To make things even worse, none of the blinds came with pre-drilled holes, and the finishing trims/accessories for the blinds were delivered almost at the very end, all together in a single package. This caused me even more problems because I had already installed some of the blinds since I needed privacy in my home urgently, and I was never informed that these finishing parts even existed.

This whole experience has been a nightmare. After 2 months of stress, excuses, delays, missing parts, and terrible customer service, I am still missing one of the blinds from my order.

I strongly advise people to avoid this company. In my opinion, customers are being misled and treated unfairly. Save yourself the stress and buy somewhere else.

I'm now going down the chargeback / ECC Ireland route to get the full €426.73 back.
Irish customers especially — be aware that post-Brexit, your protections against UK traders are not what they used to be. Spend your money somewhere that can count to four.

one_star_reviews.text: Yikes! Please don’t trust this place with your money. We’ve never had issues with other letting agents (maybe because we’re good tenants?) but Whitegates have ruined that streak. We left the house in a state far better than when we moved in (literally dirty socks stuffed down the radiator), and cleaned the carpets with a professional carpet cleaner due to having a cat in the house. We were not expecting to have £225 knocked off of our deposit but here we are. We’ve been dealing with Ellie who is now refusing to provide any evidence or documents regarding special instructions on carpet cleaning, or what kind of carpet cleaner to use etc prior to us moving in. They’re still taking off all of this money because apparently the clean carpets are not clean enough (our stuff was the good cleaning stuff - and we provided proof of that). Now I’d hold my hands up or wave a white flag if Ellie had provided this evidence to us, however - as I say - she has refused. Not very helpful! On top of that, we had someone let themselves into the house to conduct a viewing that we were never even told about, which was the cherry on top. Terrifying having 3 strangers walk in on you in the morning. I know this is a minor story compared to the other ones you’ll be reading down below, but just thought we’d add a little something. Don’t do it, guys! Don’t make our mistake!

I had a suitcase returned to my previous property managed by Whitegates at Victoria Court, Newark — it had a return to sender label on it. I had been a tenant of the property for around 15 months. The tenant left the suitcase unattended outside the flat without informing the agency (I had collection pending and the agency were aware of this) it was taken by someone unknown, and it is now gone.

I am based abroad and have no ability to investigate in person. All I asked was for Whitegates to send one email to tenants at the block asking if anyone had seen it. One email. That is the entire request.

Diane — who I understand is a director of this branch — refused. Instead she offered a notice on a board that most residents will never see, told me Whitegates would be “stepping away” from the matter, and made clear she had no intention of helping further. I have then been ignored since the 23rd April.

I have worked with property management and have dealt with letting agents across multiple Whitegates offices, primarily the Mansfield branch. The difference in professionalism is stark. In all that time I have never encountered an agent — let alone a director — so unwilling to assist with something so simple. The response was lazy, condescending, and completely unbefitting someone in a leadership position.

What makes this particularly telling is that Diane and the team clearly have no problem finding time to respond to Google reviews to polish their image — yet a director couldn’t spare two minutes to send one email to help a customer who lost hundreds of pounds of his own belongings due to a failure on their watch. That says everything about where their priorities really lie.

For a director to behave this way is not just poor customer service — it sets the tone for the entire office. Based on the reviews here, it appears this is not an isolated incident but a pattern of behaviour from the top down.

Avoid this branch entirely.

First Visit
Approximately one month ago I visited Wickes Daybrook and noted Senetti garden plants priced at £7 per pot. I raised at the till that B&M and Home Bargains, located within yards of the store, were selling the identical plants for £3.50. I asked staff to pass this to head office for a price review. No action was taken and no communication was received.
Second Visit — 22 April 2026
I returned today to find the same plants on a trolley at the front of the store in a severely deteriorated, largely dead condition. A store assistant confirmed the price remained £7 but said some were reduced. I checked the entire trolley; there were no reduced labels on any plant. Staff confirmed there were none — only the full £7 price applied.
Inconsistent Pricing
A customer ahead of me took 2 plants from the same trolley and was charged £1 each. I then took 4 plants from the same trolley and was told the price was £7 each. I queried this directly. The assistant upheld the full price without explanation. Manager Beth was called. Rather than addressing the inconsistency, Beth pointed at random plants and directed me to shop at B&M. This was dismissive and deeply embarrassing, made publicly at the front of the store.
Relevant Legislation
Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 — Regulation 5 prohibits misleading actions. Verbally representing that reduced prices existed when no discounted labels were present constitutes a false statement of price likely to cause the average consumer to make a different transactional decision. Regulation 6 further covers misleading omissions where material pricing information is withheld.
Price Marking Order 2004 — Retailers are required to display the selling price of products clearly and unambiguously. Indicating that reduced prices applied without any corresponding price labels on the items in question is non-compliant with this obligation.
Consumer Rights Act 2015 — Section 62 requires that contract terms and trading practices are fair. Applying materially different prices to 2 customers selecting identical items from the same display within moments of each other, without a lawful or transparent basis, is an unfair commercial practice.

A wholly unsatisfactory experience. That’s actually being polite.

On personal recommendation from a friend, my partner approached Ideas and asked for a home visit and consultation for a new kitchen to be fitted. She wanted a considerable amount of improvement and design work done, and was prepared to spend accordingly for a project that she was very excited about starting.

Their consultant attended my partner’s house in February this year. I was also there at the meeting. Nothing really of any concern during the hour or so he was there. He came over as enthusiastic about progressing the kitchen redesign for my partner.

He said that he would now go away and draw up the plans and costs figures for the work. It is at this point (and I’ve seen similar situations described on previous reviews about this company) that the whole thing began to go wrong. He then sent two holding type emails, neither particularly grammatically well set out, that essentially were offering various excuses as to why the plans hadn’t been sent through to her as yet. Then we had a period of total silence. Bearing in mind the consultant came round at some point in February, we had now reached later May, and she had still not had the design plans. It almost felt like they had subsequently decided that they didn’t want the work, and were just hoping that she would now not come back to them. Either that or the administration processes are absolutely hopeless.

My partner, then contacted the consultant again via email last weekend. He came back to her eventually, suggesting that she perhaps looked in her junk folder, as he couldn’t understand why his plans hadn’t been received by her. Subsequently, he contacted her again today, and with a different scenario - saying this time that the details of her kitchen requirements had now been found, but in another customer’s job folder. Essentially, you couldn’t make it up. You would have thought if, as he initially suggested, that the plans had been sent out and there was no response back from the customer, they would’ve been proactive in following up with them. We are probably talking about £30,000 to £40,000 of work and materials here, and neither of us can remotely understand how a professionally run company could allow this to happen or simply let the work just drift away like this.

My partner responded back today, basically telling him that she wanted nothing more to do with the company.

I do a lot of reviews on Google Maps, and it is always much more pleasurable to give positive feedback for good service received. Equally, when you receive terrible service, you feel that you should also share it to assist others in their decisions to which company in this case to engage to take on a potentially expensive piece of kitchen redesign work, and which not to.

Their continued delays are actively obstructing my ability to pursue corrective medical treatment and legal action following a failed private surgery in the UK which has left me with ongoing breathing problems.

For years I struggled with breathing difficulties and received little meaningful help. Eventually, out of desperation, I paid thousands of pounds privately in an attempt to improve my quality of life. The surgery went wrong, and now even the process of seeking justice and further treatment is being hindered because this GP practice refuses to cooperate with lawful requests for my records.

Gateley Smithers Purslow - we experienced appalling service,

Gateley Smithers Purslow were employed as independent surveyors in our house restoration following a fire.
The process took from 2021 to 2025 - probably about two years longer than it should.
I found them to be:
1. Technically inept, unable or unwilling to recognise obvious problems
2. Generally incompetent
3. Unable to communicate effectively, accurately or without long delays
4. Unable to produce simple schedules/reports accurately or in line with the requirements of the insurance company
5. Generally unable or unwilling to manage effectively the contract or the contractors on site, leading to long and unnecessary delays
6,. Largely unable to impartially conduct an internal investigation into my complaint against them.
7. Unwilling to listen to us, the customer, and continuously insistent on relying on paper reports/certificates instead of looking at the problems which were there and obvious before their (and everyone else's) own eyes.
This led to numerous serious problems, including leaving us with potentially dangerous electrics, a dangerous banister which could have killed us, a dangerous chimney flue etc.
8. Lazy in the extreme - that is my honest perception.
9. In denial, and unable or unwilling to accept their responsibilities as contract administrators.
10. Always looking for the cheapest remedy, despite our insurance policy which was 'like for like'.

Perhaps one example will illustrate the malaise:
Before the fire, we had solid wooden internal doors.
Our insurance was on a 'like for like' basis.
Under the watchful eyes of Gateley Smithers Purslow, the contractor replaced the upstairs doors with mdf core doors.
We pointed this out to Gateley several times, both verbally and in writing, but they ignored us - for nearly two years!
As relationships were straining, we again complained about this, again with full evidence.
The surveyor in charge, who clearly had more important things on hand, just dismissed this, saying the installed doors were in fact solid wood.
Finally, having repeatedly submitted evidence, the Gateley general manager had a light bulb moment, whereby he managed to recognise the evidence in front of his own eyes.
So, our claim was forwarded to the insurers, and we were finally paid - although of course not enough (another story).
But to cap it all, the Gateley general manager then used this as an example of how much Gateley had helped us!!!

There is so, so much more, which could probably fill a library.

I complained to RICS who investigated (took a year and a half!) and generally found for us, but decide it was not "in the public interest" to pursue disciplinary action.

Towards the end, Gateley Smithers Purslow just decided to stop communicating with us, and refused to reply to our correspondence , even though we had a signed contract in force.

I recommend never, ever, using this firm of surveyors, based on my experience with them.

If you need to use a surveyor, I would strongly recommend establishing, at the outset, PRECISELY what they think their roles and responsibilities are, and get it in writing, signed and witnessed.
Also, make sure you have an experienced project manager to watch all involved in the process like a hawk.
We thought our surveyors were there to administer the contract independently and fairly. I feel we made a dreadful error of judgement.

one_star_reviews.text:
Outdated model with excessive fees and poor value

I would not recommend St James’s Place.

My experience/opinion is that the whole model feels outdated: high charges, restricted advice, expensive funds, and performance that does not seem to justify the cost. When you compare it with a simple low-cost global tracker, the value proposition looks extremely weak.

What concerns me most is the historic fee structure. SJP has been criticised for things like high ongoing charges and early exit fees, which in my view made it harder for clients to leave once they realised they were not getting good value. That kind of model feels very old-fashioned and not aligned with what modern investors should expect.

The fees are not just slightly high. They can be astronomically high compared with low-cost alternatives, and that matters because every extra percentage point in fees compounds against the client over time. You can end up paying a premium price while still getting underwhelming performance.

To me, SJP seems to benefit from the fact that many clients do not know how cheap and simple investing can be elsewhere. Once you understand the alternatives, it is very difficult to justify paying so much for restricted advice and expensive managed funds.

In my view, this is an antiquated, poor-value wealth management model that relies far too much on complexity, trust, and client ignorance rather than genuinely superior outcomes.

I’ve had a pretty frustrating experience with Cuckoo Fibre overall, despite some positives.

To start with the good: when the connection actually works, the speeds are genuinely very good. Streaming, downloads, and general browsing are all fast and stable at times, which is what you’d hope for from a fibre provider.

However, the issues around everything else have really let it down.

Customer service has been a major pain point. It often feels like the support team doesn’t fully understand what’s being asked, even for relatively simple requests. On multiple occasions, I’ve tried to get straightforward changes made and it’s either taken far too long or hasn’t been done correctly at all.

A big limitation is the lack of control over the router. You can’t make basic network changes yourself — things like opening ports, changing the WiFi password, or even renaming your network. This is incredibly restrictive, especially if you have smart home devices, gaming setups, or anything that requires port forwarding or custom configuration. Most providers allow at least some level of user control, so this feels unnecessarily locked down.

I’ve also had ongoing issues with devices struggling to connect reliably. There have been multiple engineer visits, and while they’ve confirmed there is a problem, no one seems able to identify the root cause. To make matters worse, the engineers aren’t directly employed by Cuckoo, so there’s a bit of a disconnect in accountability and follow-up.

On the administrative side, things haven’t been much better. I submitted a subject access request over 2.5 months ago and am still waiting for a response, which is well beyond expected timeframes. Formal complaints also seem to disappear into a void — I’m told responses have been sent, but I’ve never actually received them.

In summary, while the raw internet speeds are strong, the lack of router control, poor customer support, unresolved technical issues, and slow (or nonexistent) responses to formal requests make this a difficult service to recommend.

In 2022, I was informed that there was a place at a theology college, with an added chance to increase my HSC qualifications.

I loved worshipping in the mornings, I did feel that D the project leader could of tried a bit better than trying to make out that he was a superstar preacher, when all he was doing was being lazy, he never knew that I clocked that he was just reading passages from the Word for Today.
Although I enjoyed the classes, I started to recognise after a few weeks, that it wasn't the theology college that they had told me that it was, it was a large homeless shelter.
At the time, they were busy 'fixing up' as many rooms as they could, in the expectation of getting 100's of 1000's of pounds from the government for housing Ukrainians, it was clear that it wasn't from the heart, it was greed, their was a strange atmosphere around the place, certainly not of the Lord. The Lord won't be mocked, He of course cancelled it through their greed.
I kept my mouth shut, trying to dig deeper into the Word.
There was a lot of drugs being taken in the place, but I noticed that D would overlook some doing it but throwing out some people, it was always vulnerable people that he threw out. One individual came back absolutely off his head after going missing on a session from Friday to Monday, he was told to go to bed and sleep it off.
They were making a lot of money from the government, taking in early release prisoners etc.
The atmosphere can be very toxic in there, one day, I had a minor disagreement with someone, I needed to breathe and not get angry, so I got myself out of the way for a while.
To my disbelief, coming back after a few hours, most of my clothes and some of my belongings were strewn across the road in front of the entrance to the college.
D was like a rabid dog, obviously my face didn't fit, he told me that I couldn't come back in. It was so cruel, it was beyond belief, I had nowhere to go, as I had given everything up, no matter how I tried to explain this, he said no.

Many staff members got in touch with me, disgusted at what he had done to me.
I was now homeless on the streets for the first time, which lasted many months, because D was terrified of me taking legal action, telling the council that I had left, so they said "as i had left voluntarily, they couldn't help me".

If you are thinking of going here, be warned, I speak with sincerity and truth, it is NOT a college, it is a money spinning homeless shelter, be aware of the puffed up pride from the project leader, if your face doesn't fit, you should expect to be treated as I was.

Vehicle Dispute Complicated by Business Bankruptcy. We purchased a car from National Car Finder in December 2025 via a fully remote sale. Shortly after delivery, we identified dampness in the boot area, signs of moisture near electrical components, and the vehicle also later developed an issue with the boot latch mechanism.

We also discovered that some of the information provided to us before purchase did not align with the V5C documentation we later received. The vehicle had been described to us as having one previous owner; however, the V5C showed us as the third registered keeper.

We raised these concerns promptly and requested to return the vehicle for a refund, but this was not agreed to. We subsequently commenced the small claims process based on our understanding of rights relating to remote sales under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 and vehicle quality requirements under the Consumer Rights Act 2015.

During this process, we became aware that the business owner had entered bankruptcy. This significantly affected how the matter could progress and what practical resolution options remain available to us. Details are publicly available via the UK Insolvency Register.

We are also still awaiting the service book that we were told would be supplied. In addition, despite twice requesting that photographs be removed from social media, these remain visible after our request.

Based on our experience, we would strongly encourage prospective buyers to carry out thorough due diligence before proceeding with a purchase, including carefully reviewing documentation, requesting full terms and conditions in advance, and inspecting any vehicle in person before making payment. Buyers may also wish to consider using a payment method that provides additional consumer protection where available, such as a credit card.

I booked a chassis inspection via WhatsApp in advance. The first thing I was greeted with upon arrival was:
"What do you want?"

I explained that I had an appointment, and the response was:
“You booked to lift the car and check it?”

Since I didn’t record the conversation, here are the most memorable parts:
1. “Why do you need to lift the car to check?”
(The tone felt more like an interrogation than a service conversation. Honestly caught me off guard.)
2. I explained:
I’m not very familiar with cars, and I’ve noticed some unusual noises and sensations. Since the car is still under warranty, I wanted to check if there’s any issue with the chassis.
3. The reply:
“If there’s a problem, why don’t you just go back to the manufacturer? Even if I find something, they might still say there’s no issue and refuse to fix it. Don’t waste everyone’s time here.”

At that moment, I recalled that this inspection is actually a paid service.
Apparently, even when you’re paying, it can still be considered “a waste of time.”

This really made me rethink life —
Maybe I should tell my boss: “Let’s not waste each other’s time, I’ll just stop working.” 🧐

I engaged with Savills Shepherd's Bush regarding a property at Caxton Gate in late 2025/early 2026. The property was marketed as "new build" when it was actually a conversion completed in 2022. The property "should not have been described as new build"
Required documents "were supplied to Savills but not provided to" me
My experience "fell short of expected standards"

Despite these admissions, Savills offered only £500 compensation. I escalated to the Property Redress Scheme (case PRSC120583), which upheld the £500 award and Savills has now paid this compensation.
The complaint is public record (reference PRSC120583). Prospective buyers should:

Verify all marketing claims independently
Request all material documents upfront
Document everything in writing
Be aware that "new build" may mean "conversion"

SDL were instructed by YBS to complete the valuation of our property, and we paid £229 to cover the cost of a level two homebuyer survey.

The Homebuyer Survey should include a visual inspection of all major features including ceilings, roof, walls, and bathrooms, as well as permanent outdoor buildings and features including roofing, pipes, gutters, walls, windows, and doors.

To say it was a waste of money is an understatement.

They gave our main roof a condition rating of 2, stated there were a few broken tiles and some which has been replaced. After a few broken tiles fell onto our drive, a roofing contractor told me that the condition of the roof from ground level inspection alone was appalling. Upon greater inspection we had over 50 broken tiles, some tiles glued together with adhesive, guttering that was filled with rubble and broken tiles, and ridge tiles being held in place by friction alone. Our roof should have never been given a good or satisfactory rating and is in fact in need of urgent repair. We have since had to fork out over £9,396 for a new main roof. There goes the bathroom renovation.

We then discovered that the roof on the extension of the property (given a condition rating of 1) had the incorrect tiles installed for the pitch of the roof. Again, a qualified (and decent surveyor) would have been able to make this conclusion from eye level. It's a matter of time before damp and leakage issues occur through the VELUX windows because of the pitch, and we are looking at over £6000 to have this roof re-pitched and replaced too, aswell as over £1000 for new VELUX windows.

Not to mention, the surveyor completely missed a hole in the side of our exterior wall, from an old soil pipe. We are again, having to fork out over £1,000 to get this fixed and we don't know if further damp issues are going to arise.

We would not have purchased the property had SDL's survey been accurate. I requested the site notes and photographs and SDL refused to release them (which is one, illegal as we paid for the service, and two either demonstrates that the photos show that the damage was there or no sufficient photographs or site notes were taken by the individual who inspected the property).

All they have been prepared to offer us was a £250 'good will' gesture which covers some of what we paid for the survey - nothing more.

I also reported them to their governing body. But as their terms and conditions state sometimes mistakes are made and things are missed - they legally completely get around situations like ours.

As first time home buyers we have been unable to move into the property until building work is completed and it has shattered our experience of buying our first home.

Avoid SDL at all costs. Just get a builder, electrician & roofer you trust to inspect your property so you know exactly what you’re getting yourself into.

one_star_reviews.text:
I bought my BMW from Evans Halshaw on Saturday, 18th April, after visiting on a whim to see if the car would suit me. After spending a couple of hours with the salesperson, Will, I decided it was the right car for me. We agreed on a price, and I took it for a test drive. Initially, the car drove well, but once I got onto a dual carriageway, it felt slightly sluggish. As I had never driven an automatic before and was coming from a 2.3-litre car, I assumed this was something I would simply need to adjust to. The sales manager and Will also took the car on a separate drive and agreed.

However, after driving the car for a few hours, I began receiving repeated battery fault notifications both in the car and through the BMW app. I contacted Evans Halshaw on Monday, less than 48 hours after purchase, but was initially told they couldn’t inspect the car until Friday. After explaining that I urgently needed the issue resolved as I was going away for the weekend, they agreed to see the car on Wednesday. By 5pm that day, they confirmed it was a battery fault and they needed Sales to approve a battery replacement.

As It was just a simple battery fault I was told it would be complete for Friday tea time. i left the car with them for repair and planned to collect it on Friday. When I called on Friday for an update, I was told the replacement part had been ordered but had not yet arrived, and I was promised a callback within an hour. No one called back, and when I attempted to contact them again at 5pm, despite the dealership being open until 6pm, my calls went unanswered. I ended up taking the train as I couldn’t contact the dealership.

On Monday morning, I called again, only to be told that the battery had not actually been ordered because sales had not yet approved the replacement cost. I explained that I urgently needed the car back as I was travelling for work on Tuesday. Later that day, I was informed the car should be ready by teatime. However, when I arrived to collect it, the same error message was still present. I had no choice but to leave the car with them once more, and I was told they would investigate further on Tuesday.

Because I was travelling for work on Tuesday and still had no functioning vehicle, I was forced to arrange alternative transport. Eventually, I was informed that there was supposedly nothing wrong with the car and that the BMW app was simply unreliable, with the error message expected to disappear on its own.

When someone collected the car for me, it was returned in an unacceptable condition — filthy, covered in dust and tree sap. I had already paid for a full valet on the day of purchase because the dealership had not cleaned the vehicle before handing it over which I was accepting off given the price offered to me, and now I am forced to pay for it to be cleaned again despite barely being driven.

Overall, my experience with Evans Halshaw’s after-sales service has been extremely disappointing. Communication was poor throughout, promises were repeatedly broken, calls went unanswered, and I was left without a reliable vehicle despite purchasing it only days earlier. This situation has already cost me over £200 in travel expenses alone, not including valeting costs, and I am still dealing with the same unresolved app error. Based on my experience, I would strongly caution others against purchasing a vehicle from this dealership.

**
I emailed the address provided on the date the response was posted, but I still haven’t received a reply. Evans Halshaw appears to be quick to take your money but offers very little care or support when it comes to after-sales service. My final thought from above very much still stands. I would strongly caution others against purchasing a vehicle from this dealership.

This is the third time I have dealt with poor customer service from Evans Halshaw and after using them for over 9 years I expected better and as soon as the opportunity arises I will be ending my agreement with them.
I also have two family members who have had faulty C3's sold to them from the same branch; they will also be terminating their agreements at the next available opportunity.

Avoid! Just after your money!!

one_star_reviews.text:
One star as zero wasn't available.

Don't get ill in Lincoln whatever you do.

Shocking experience, made to crawl on the floor due to being unable to walk, no wheelchairs, prescription for pain relief incorrectly written therefore could not be dispensed, refused xray because back pain isn’t taken seriously, even after a fall with osteoarthritis.  Left in pain, cannot return to obtain correct prescription, watched a nurse mock an elderly patient.

The worst hospital ever, they almost killed my mom, three times infection because of their negligence, discrimination and appaling management. Waited for 10 hours just to get a bad so the doctor would finaly see my mom in three days when she clearly had severe infection.

I was sat there for 7 hours in agony with no pain relief, this was after being seen. I was forgotten and left there literally crying with no help or assistance. nurses that did see me were lovely tho.

One star is generous, and the only reason Lincoln County Hospital is receiving it is due to the care I eventually received from staff on the Urgent Medical Assessment Unit, who were kind and doing their best in very difficult circumstances.

I attended A&E at 6:55am on Wednesday due to four days of continuous vomiting and clear signs of severe dehydration. Despite being visibly unwell and actively vomiting, I waited to be acknowledged at reception.

After initial triage, I was taken for bloods and a cannula. The procedure was carried out roughly, causing significant pain and bruising. I was then sent back to the waiting area.

By 11am, I had still not been seen by a doctor. I was severely dehydrated and continuously vomiting, yet I was not given IV fluids or effective anti-sickness treatment during this time. I was told waits could be up to 7 hours. There was also a complete lack of dignity, being left to vomit repeatedly in a public waiting area.

I was finally seen by a doctor around 5pm (approximately 10 hours later), who confirmed I was severely dehydrated and required IV fluids and a CT scan. Despite this, after initial treatment I was left for long periods without monitoring, further fluids, or reassessment, while still being unwell and unable to keep fluids down.

I was told I needed admission but there were no beds available. At around 2am, I was moved to a “ward”, which was in fact a crowded room with multiple patients in chairs rather than beds. The environment was extremely noisy and not appropriate for patients requiring rest and recovery.

I do want to acknowledge that there was one nurse in A&E who was genuinely caring and hardworking. She was clearly being pulled from pillar to post and expected to do far more than one person should, while others appeared far less engaged. Unfortunately, I did not get her name, but she stood out for all the right reasons.

The conditions in A&E were also concerning. I observed poor cleanliness, including dried blood on the floor. There appeared to be a lack of basic care and oversight, with vulnerable patients left waiting prolonged periods without assistance.

One particularly concerning incident involved an elderly patient whose catheter was visibly full of blood and not draining. Despite asking multiple staff members for help, no one returned. I felt compelled to intervene and raise this myself.

I also witnessed unsafe moving and handling practices, including patients being dragged under the arms, which raises serious concerns about patient safety.

The overall environment was chaotic, with patients left without appropriate seating, some sitting on the floor, and a general lack of organisation and dignity.

While I appreciate the pressure NHS staff are under, the level of care, safety, and basic standards I experienced and witnessed was not acceptable.

I will be raising a formal complaint regarding both my care and the wider issues observed

On the plus side, the Ambulance crew were fantastic and the initial assessment at the hospital was quick. But then we became part of the slow drawn out process occurring in this emergency department. The whole process, in particular the long waits to be treated and lack of information on what’s happening appear designed to encourage patients to give up waiting and discharge themselves (which we have done more than once). The department is too small for the number of patients it attempts to treat, out of its depth and is not fit for purpose. Based on our recent visits to this department, most nights there are a dozen or more patients that have been waiting two to three  days for a bed. And whilst waiting these often very poorly patients are basically ignored and left to fend for themselves.  For these patients stuck waiting for beds for days on end, there are no facilities for showering offered, no hot meals , overused filthy toilets and noise to keep them awake twenty four hours a day. You might say why don’t the patients that have long waits just pop home to eat and wash whilst waiting for a bed, blood test or scan result, but NO !! NHS rules state you can’t leave the emergency department- if you do you have effectively discharged yourself, and when and if you return your care within the department has been reset so you have to start all over again with an initial assessment followed by endless waits.
Some of the staff are very poorly trained with attitudes where they expect the patient to fend for themselves - whatever happened to the caring profession? Very few auxiliary staff provide even basic care. Whoever is in charge of the nursing staff of Lincoln A&E is failing in their responsibilities. And whoever in admin decided to process patients the way they are dealt with needs to look themselves in the mirror. Yes we are bitter that things have got so bad we would rather risk staying away from this emergency department rather than try to be treated by this emergency department. What choice do we have but to look outside of Lincolnshire for an A&E that provides a proper service where patients are treated as human beings, not  cogs in a go-as-slow-as-possible soulless machine that is Lincoln A&E.

Review of TLScontact Nottingham – Poor Customer Service Experience

I had a very disappointing experience at TLScontact Nottingham during our appointment on 10 April 2026 at 09:15. I arrived on time at 09:00 with my three young children (ages 7, 3, and 1), traveling all the way from New Ollerton.

Upon arrival, we were asked by a floor staff member to go back downstairs and return after 15 minutes because other appointments were still ongoing. While I understand delays can happen, this was inconvenient, especially with three small children.

When we returned at 09:15 and entered the office, the floor staff directed us to sit, but their tone and attitude lacked warmth and understanding. There was no consideration for the fact that I was managing three young children. My 3-year-old child was crying and very uncomfortable, which made the situation even more stressful.

What was most upsetting was that because my child was crying, I was told that I might need to cancel the appointment and come back another day. This was extremely frustrating and unreasonable. Managing young children is not easy, and instead of offering support or patience, the staff added more stress to an already difficult situation.

In addition, the appointment was significantly delayed, and due to the late processing, I was forced to cancel my child’s GP appointment. This caused further inconvenience and disruption to our day.

The floor staff behaved in an unprofessional and dismissive manner. Their approach felt overly strict and lacked basic customer service skills. As a third-party service provider, they should be more understanding and better trained to handle families, especially those with young children.

However, I would like to highlight that the biometric officer who assisted my 3-year-old daughter was very kind, calm, and professional. She made both me and my child feel comfortable during the process. Unfortunately, I do not remember her name, but she was seated near the office door. She was the only positive part of this experience.

TLScontact Nottingham seriously needs to improve staff training, especially in customer care and handling families with children.

We had a summer house supplied and installed by Waltons in April 2025. Within a matter of weeks it became clear that the build quality and installation were not to an acceptable standard.

By July 2025, the roof was leaking significantly. Before arranging repairs, we observed that water was pooling on the roof rather than draining away, which strongly indicates that the structure had not been assembled with the correct pitch to allow proper runoff. This is a fundamental installation issue. Despite this, Waltons refused to honour the warranty. They attributed the problem to nearby trees and suggested that moisture from foliage had caused water build-up. This explanation was unreasonable given that they installed the building in that exact location and the issue arose during summer conditions.

As a result of their refusal to take responsibility, we were forced to pay £1,500 for an independent contractor to properly seal the roof and resolve the issue.

In October 2025, both doors had dropped to the point where they were extremely difficult to open and close. Waltons did attend on this occasion and replaced the doors, adjusting the hinges higher in an attempt to correct the problem. We followed all advice provided, including applying appropriate weatherproof treatments.

However, by April 2026, the same issue has occurred again. The replacement doors have also dropped and are sticking badly. Despite this being a repeat fault, Waltons have now refused to attend altogether. They have stated that the issue is weather related and advised that the building needs to be aired regularly to prevent movement. This is not a credible explanation given that the structure is used as a home office and is opened and ventilated five days a week.

Across every stage of this experience, there has been a consistent pattern of poor workmanship, questionable installation standards, and a complete reluctance to stand behind their product. The warranty has proven to be effectively meaningless, with responsibility avoided at every opportunity.

Based on our experience, the materials are of low quality, the installation was flawed from the outset, and the aftercare has been wholly inadequate.

They had to ring around the garages they use to find out where it was and it turned out to be 2 hours away sat in someone else's garage! In just over a month it was back with me after being told it was fixed and them kindly leaving me invoices in the car to see for myself, but this wasn't the case.

The same issues were still very much there, so I contacted the finance company and advised them I wished to reject the car as it was costing me further money to run with constantly topping up with oil and ultimately was sold to me in a faulty state.

The Car Arena then contacted me stating they would fix it but they had tried that once and I had no trust or faith in them. Plus I didn't know how long they would have it or if they'd misplace it again..I just wanted rid. They clearly weren't happy with this because the arrogance and rudeness each time I spoke to them was unreal.

The finance company independently assessed the car and agreed this car had been sold to me in a faulty manner and my rejection was accepted. The Car Arena came and collected the car and I was refunded by the finance company. All apart from my deposit which was the Car Arena's responsibility to refund. They wanted the log book, understandably and which I then posted seperately. They confirmed they had received this and would refund my deposit. I was then told that this had been done and would take a few days to clear which turned out to be yet another lie. They had not done this then had the audacity to ask me for an invoice confirming the amount I had paid, a week after stating they had processed the refund. Pretty typical of them to be honest.

I had to take it upon myself to remind them that business' should keep financial records for 6 years and therefore should have a copy of my invoice along with threatening to take them to small claims court if the money wasnt refunded by a date I provided and sure enough the money dropped in my account.

My advice to anyone is avoid this garage at all costs. They lie constantly, clearly dont check cars and only want your money.

Dont waste your time with them, look elsewhere. Absolute cowboys who dont deserve to be a business.

My experience with this garage was extremely poor, with repeated dishonesty and serious issues with the vehicle.
I placed a deposit on a white Vauxhall Grandland X on 24th March and explained I needed it before 30 March. I was assured it would be ready. On 30 March, I was told it would be ready at 3pm, but after multiple calls and delays, I arrived to find the car wasn’t even MOT’d. I requested a refund due to the wasted time but was persuaded to continue with a promise of a 6-month warranty and a confirmed collection date of 3rd April. Despite further assurances, the car still wasn’t ready on collection day. I waited two hours while someone was speeding it in and out of the forecourt rushing to get it cleaned before finally taking it at 4pm.

Within two days, the car developed a loud knocking noise. An independent mechanic found a major oil leak, a snapped and rusted coil spring, and a CV joint boot (which failed on the MOT) temporarily fixed with cable ties. I also confirmed that the garage had been informed of the oil leak before sale but chose to ignore it.

I returned the car after just one week and requested a full refund. Shak, who sold me the car via the car arena, was initially refusing. He clearly has no idea about the consumer rights act, but I eventually received it. The car was relisted for sale within three days.

I strongly recommend having any vehicle from this garage independently inspected before purchase. My only positive is Simon the sales advisor is lovely and tries to go above and beyond for the customers. It's a shame the other guys don't.
