Staggering incompetence — BillyOh / Garden Buildings Direct should be avoided at all costs

BillyOh and Garden Buildings Direct are, without exaggeration, one of the most incompetent companies I have ever dealt with.

The product supplied arrived with missing and incorrect components, making assembly near impossible from the outset. This alone would be bad enough — but it was only the beginning.

The manual was incomplete, contained multiple errors and referenced parts that didn't exist.
The part IDs were incorrect or missing, didn’t match what was supplied, or bore no relation to reality. This turned what should have been a straightforward build into an absurd exercise in confusion and wasted time. A company that cannot correctly identify its own parts has no business selling self-assembly products.

Customer service was nothing short of useless. Instead of acknowledging their errors, they hid behind copy-and-paste responses, repeatedly asking for Part IDs of items that had no Part ID.

I provided a comprehensive list of every Part that had either issues with the Part or was missing entirely.
I used the Manual's Part ID which used Letters to make it easy for them to identify because not everything has a Part ID number. Yet 8 emails in they're still asking me to confirm Part IDs for items that Part IDs don't exist for!

After 8 emails I said they must have a different manual to the one they provide customers, at which point they said the manual isn't specific to the product I ordered so things might be different.
Not he manual is very clearly titled the product name and product ID with Options, it's the correct manual it's just absolute rubbish.

After that email they sent an update Part ID List and asked that I check that list instead, what company does that?!
Surprise, surprise, the new Pard ID List still didn't contain the Part ID of every item so what did they then ask for? "Please provide the Part ID" You can't make this level of incompetency up!
Responsibility has been avoided at every turn. No ownership. No urgency. No competence. Just delay, deflection, and indifference.

This is not a small mistake or an unlucky order — it is a systemic failure across quality control, documentation, logistics, and customer support. I really wish I had looked up BillyOh and Garden Buildings Direct on Trustpilot before I ordered but i foolishly assumed they were reputable.

The experience gives the clear impression that once payment is taken, the customer is an inconvenience rather than a priority.

BillyOh and Garden Buildings Direct don’t just sell garden buildings — they sell frustration, wasted weekends, and unresolved problems. If you are considering buying from them, don’t. Save yourself the stress and take your money to a company that can at least supply the correct parts with the correct instructions and the bare minimum of customer service.

This has been an astonishingly bad experience, and one I would never willingly repeat.

I am extremely disappointed with both the product quality and customer service provided by this company.

We purchased a new Wendy house supplied in multiple parts. While each bag included a parts list, the contents were completely mixed, requiring us to open every bag and manually measure components to identify them. This made the initial stages unnecessarily time-consuming.

The quality of the wood was highly inconsistent. Some pieces appeared new and well-finished, while others looked as though they had been stored in damp conditions for an extended period. In addition, several components did not match the dimensions stated in the instructions. Some key structural beams were warped or incorrectly cut, resulting in an uneven overall construction.

No printed instructions were provided—only an online manual. This made assembly more difficult, as I had to repeatedly scroll through the document on my phone to locate part dimensions for each step.

The most significant issue arose during roof assembly. The instructions specify roof boards at 143mm in width; however, all supplied boards were approximately 20mm shorter. This prevented the required overhang from being formed, making the next stage of construction impossible.

Additionally, the supplied screws were insufficient to complete even half of the build, forcing me to purchase additional materials at my own expense.

I contacted customer service to resolve these issues. The process itself was frustrating—image uploads were limited to 10MB per file, and despite being advised I could upload multiple images in one ticket, the system only allowed one per submission. I was then instructed to create multiple tickets, which was both inefficient and time-consuming.

After reviewing my evidence, the company acknowledged some parts were substandard but claimed this would not affect structural integrity. They agreed to send replacement roof boards and additional screws. However, the replacements were also incorrect (still undersized), and the quantity of screws provided was insufficient.

When I raised this again, I received inconsistent and contradictory responses. At one point, I was told that smaller boards may be sent if correct ones are out of stock, and that I should simply use more of them to compensate. This does not align with the design specifications and does not resolve the issue of the missing overhang.

At this stage, I requested a full refund and return. I was informed that I would need to cover the return shipping costs, despite the product being faulty and incomplete.

In summary, I received a product that was of poor quality, incorrectly specified, and incomplete. The customer service experience only added to the frustration, with unclear guidance and inadequate resolutions offered.

I would strongly advise others to consider alternative suppliers.

Neither a tea room or a coffeeshop, but a throwback to a hospital WRVS of the 1970s. They actually have a proper espresso machine, but the coffee tastes very old and cheap, to the point where instant coffee would probably taste nicer.

Although they sell an extra espresso, ordering a double macchiato, or a macchiato with an extra shot (whichever they understood) was met with stone blank resentment and determination not to comply. The gardens themselves were fabulous, and they do a service where they drive disabled people up from the car park to the main house in an open topped electric person carrier.

Avoid the cafe thing, it's lost in time somewhere fifty years ago. But the gardens are gorgeous.

During the procedure, the volume of the music was lowered only when the MRI machine was noisy — not when it was silent. It surely didn't look like it was a coincidence and made the already uncomfortable experience even worse.

This whole experience felt very unprofessional, uncomfortable, and poorly managed. I truly expected a much more professional and supportive environment given the sensitive nature of MRIs.

I agreed to purchase a property marketed by Richard Watkinson and was explicitly informed at the time of my offer that there was no onward chain with the sellers purchase, with an expected completion date of end of February 2026.

I was also told that the sellers’ onward purchase was already built, ready to move into, and that they were even buying furniture for it—further reinforcing that there would be no delays.

Based on this, I proceeded in good faith—spending over £1,000 on expedited searches and surveys to meet the proposed timeline, and making personal arrangements accordingly.

However, after several months, I was informed that there was in fact a chain involved. From that point on, I was given a series of inconsistent and changing completion dates (June, then May, then August), with no clear or reliable communication.

On 1st May 2026, I was finally told that the chain had collapsed entirely and the property was no longer in a position to be sold.

As a direct result of relying on the information provided, I have incurred significant financial costs and have now been left without accommodation and effectively homeless.

This situation suggests that Richard Watkinson either failed to properly establish the chain status at the outset or communicated inaccurate information throughout the process. I would strongly advise others to steer well clear of these agents as they are clearly incapable of providing a service which should be standard by an established estate agent

Purchased a used a approved AMG from the Nottingham Group 1 via distance selling. Everything went well until 5 minutes after delivery. Upon first glance, 3 of the 4 wheels that had apparently been 'fully refurbished' all had curb damage. Popped the bonnet to check the engine and to my surprise, the bonnet struts had failed resulting in the the bonnet crashing down on my head. Reported this to the sales advisor immediately who suggested they would send someone to collect the car, driving it back to Nottingham and then back to me, a 200 mile round trip on a car I had only just purchased. The day after delivery, once the rain had stopped, I wiped the car down to check the paintwork to find laquer peel across the back bumper, this was also reported. After refusing the car to be driven back to Nottingham, they reluctantly agreed to recover it. This left me without the car I had just purchased for nearly a week and without transport. On return, the bonnet struts had been replaced, however the wheels had been poorly repaired and the paintwork which I expected to be resprayed, had simply been wet sanded and polished, leaving the outline of the peeled laquer still visible. After losing faith and reporting this to the dealer, a good will gesture was offered amd accepted. A week later, upon reviewing the service history, I discovered the differential service had been missed prior to sale and was out by approximately 7300 miles. This was raised as a formal complaint and once they accepted responsibility they once again attempted to send someone to collect the car and drive it back to nottingham. I repeated my comment from the first time this was suggested, especially since a high risk item like a differential certainly shouldnt be driven all the way back.  They offered to complete the service at my nearest branch, I opted to have it done at a specialist whilst also having the gearbox service done which was also needed. Group 1 then re-embursed the cost of the service.
Fast forward 2 months and the performance exhaust developed a rattle (a very common problem) bearing on mind I am still within the 6 months Consumer protection period, group 1 inspect the car and suggest that manufacturers guidance is to 'grease' the area. Anyone who knows about these cars knows this is a maintenance approach and not a permanent fix. I refused this point blank and then was ignored for long periods. Bearing in mind, the pre inspection report I received with the car stated the exhaust to be green (perfect working order).
Group 1 have now refused to replace the section of the exhaust which is the only guaranteed fix. To add insult to injury, they offered to buy back the car a at a usage per mile rate of £1.57!!!!! Official guidance is 25p to 45p per mile!!!! I have only covered 1200 miles in 5 months!!!! This is now in the hands of the Ombudsman. No doubt customer services will reply to this review with their copy and paste comment of 'sorry you have experienced this' which is pathetic. I'm half tempted to upload all the email correspondence admitting Liability for all the faults mentioned above. Easily the worst car buying experience of my life and I certainly won't be buying a car by distance selling ever again. Buyers beware!!!

I am extremely disappointed with Appliance City and how they have handled what is clearly a serious fault.
I purchased a washing machine in November 2025 which has had a defective door from the very beginning. The door does not close properly, feels loose, and during operation it visibly moves in and out. Even more concerning, while the door is supposedly locked, it can be pulled open by approximately 2 cm. Under load, it leaks water from the bottom of the door and vibrates heavily during spin. This is not a minor issue or wear and tear—it is a fundamental failure of the door locking and sealing system on a relatively new appliance.
This has now become a genuine safety concern. I live in a household where both occupants are disabled—one is a wheelchair user and the other relies on walking sticks. Water leaking onto the floor creates a very real and dangerous slip hazard. An appliance that introduces that level of risk is clearly not fit for purpose, and it is deeply concerning that this has not been treated with urgency.
Despite clearly explaining the issue and providing video evidence, Appliance City have failed to take proper responsibility. Instead of addressing the problem as the retailer, they have repeatedly attempted to deflect the issue onto the manufacturer and hide behind internal processes, suggesting that nothing can be done without manufacturer involvement. This is simply incorrect and shows either a lack of understanding of consumer rights or a deliberate attempt to avoid dealing with the issue.
Communication has been slow and unhelpful, with a clear lack of urgency despite the safety implications. I have effectively been left chasing responses while dealing with a faulty and potentially unsafe appliance in my home.
For a product that was not cheap, and a fault that has been present since new, this level of service is unacceptable. When something goes wrong, you expect a company to step up and resolve it properly. In this case, Appliance City have done the opposite.
I would strongly advise others to think twice before purchasing from Appliance City. If something goes wrong, you may find yourself having to fight to get them to take even basic responsibility.

I rarely leave reviews, but this experience has been unacceptable from start to finish.
I instructed Shergroup to enforce a High Court writ. From the outset, communication was poor. I received little to no meaningful updates unless I repeatedly chased, and even then responses were inconsistent. I was passed between staff and promised callbacks that did not happen.
Enforcement eventually succeeded and the debtor made payment by card on 9 April 2026. I was advised the funds would clear within 3 to 5 working days. However, I was not proactively updated when this happened. I had to chase Shergroup on 16 April 2026 to ask what was happening, and only then was I told that the funds had actually cleared into their client account on 14 April 2026.
It was also only after I chased that I was then informed, for the first time, that the funds would be held for a further 28 days. This had never been explained at the outset and no clear legal basis was provided. There is no stay of enforcement in place and no formal application to set aside has been served.
At the point of writing, my funds remain withheld despite enforcement being complete and despite the money having already cleared into their account. The delay, poor communication and lack of transparency have caused unnecessary and avoidable financial stress.
For a regulated firm handling High Court enforcement, the standard of communication and client handling has fallen well below what should reasonably be expected.
Based on my experience, I would not recommend this firm.

Update after the reply:  In response to the owner’s reply, I need to clarify a few factual points.
I have not spoken to anyone called “Sue”, and I do not know who that refers to. Since last week, I have not received any meaningful update unless I have chased repeatedly.
I have not had a consistent point of contact. I am repeatedly told someone will deal with the issue, then communication changes again. This lack of continuity and follow‑through has been a constant problem throughout.
I was informed in writing that funds would be held for 28 days, not 14, and this was only explained after I chased following clearance. This was not explained at the outset.
For a firm acting as High Court Enforcement Officers, the level of communication, clarity, and consistency I have experienced has been extremely poor.

We have visited this café multiple times specifically because of the children’s play area, which is very important for my daughter, who has additional needs. Having a safe and engaging space like this makes a big difference for her.
Unfortunately, on both occasions, the experience has been disappointing.
The first time, we were told quite abruptly that the area was off limits, with no clear explanation. During our most recent visit, we made a point of asking before ordering whether we could sit in the play area and were told that we could. However, shortly after, the area was once again blocked off with chairs and we were told it was being cleaned.
When I explained that we had come specifically for that space and that this had happened before, I was met with a dismissive response, being told that it was not their fault and that they were trying to go home. This felt unprofessional and lacking in understanding.
What made the situation more upsetting was that my daughter, who already finds changes and disappointment difficult, became very distressed when she realised she couldn’t access the area she had been looking forward to. It was also confusing to see other customers accessing and sitting in the same space without being approached, which made the situation feel inconsistent and unfair.
I completely understand the need for cleaning and closing procedures, but clearer communication and a more consistent approach would make a significant difference,especially for families like ours who rely on these facilities.
At the moment, this experience makes it difficult for us to feel confident returning.

one_star_reviews.text: Just like so many shops nowadays have to have an app or a store card to get the actual price displayed, no wonder I usually go to the Range nowadays.

Leaving this to protect others from the poor experience I had with Life and Dream Conversions, which contrasts the overwhelmingly positive reviews visible online.

Initially, I approached Life and Dream conversions for exterior Raptor spray work, a supplied and fitted awning, and a complete off-grid electrical system. The company promotes itself as a "one-stop shop" for full camper conversions, which gave me confidence. Unfortunately, the issues began early on.

The spray job was botched from the start—done in cold weather and clearly not in a proper spray booth. This caused delays and required  further work. Upon collection, sawdust was being blown over and into the van as final work was still happening, which didn’t inspire confidence. Martin dodged questions about the paintwork and told me to inspect it again after cleaning it in a few weeks.

Driving away, I realized the speedometer wasn’t working. Martin later admitted they had removed and discarded the factory-fitted tachograph, which was responsible for the speedo function. More issues quickly emerged—my rear and side doors no longer locked properly or functioned as they had before, compromising security. Martin downplayed the problem, offering no urgency despite £3,000+ worth of equipment now unsecured inside.

I also noticed that the awning looked odd. It turned out the wrong size (2.6m) had been fitted for my L2H2 Ducato. The proper size should have been 3.2m and attached using existing fixings, but instead, they used pretruding brackets drilled in. Kerry acknowledged this mistake and promised a replacement, along with other rectifications, including a respray with a hired booth.

After cleaning the van, I was gutted. The Raptor paintwork was full of gritty patches, missed spots, runs, overspray, visible rust, and damage from tools—far from the protective, durable finish expected. Concerned, I consulted a Raptor specialist who confirmed the poor prep, minimal coating, and substandard results, describing it as nothing more than a "base coat" with inadequate protection.

I had initially been happy with the electrical work, but for peace of mind, I brought in a qualified auto electrician. His verdict: the system was unsafe, lacked basic RCD protection, and had solar panels fitted using wood screws and furniture brackets—dangerously inadequate. He estimated over £2,000 would be needed to correct it. A local garage also laughed at the damaged door mechanisms and poorly reinstalled rear step.

Throughout the process, Martin would pressure me for payments before work had been properly inspected, often citing staff wages, signs of possible cash flow issues. Sadly I fell for these and acted in good faith to help a small business.

Ultimately, I decided not to return the van for rectification. I’d lost all confidence. over £10,000 out of pocket and climbing, with a van that’s unsafe and worse off than when it arrived. I tried to proceed with at least swapping the awning, but Martin never responded on the many occasions I made contact about this. Most disturbingly, he later disputed the professional electrical findings rather than taking responsibility—revealing a dangerous mix of overconfidence and incompetence blurring liens between stupidity and arrogance.

This experience has taught me hard lessons: never pay in full before inspecting work, and be wary of overly glowing reviews—many of which, I suspect, may have been submitted by friends/ employees.

In my opinion, Martin and Life and Dream lack the skills, facilities, and professionalism to deliver safe or high-quality van conversions. The potential danger of poor electrical work should not be understated. Until these serious issues are acknowledged and corrected, I cannot reccomend life and dream conversions.

*UPDATE* Have since had work done to the VAN and our electrician has found concealed cables twisted together throughout the build including the DC to DC Cable which was two Solar Cables strapped together.. Absolute Fraud.

I feel compelled to share our recent experience.

My 19-year-old daughter attended Highbury Dental Care in severe pain with visible facial swelling. When booking the appointment, I clearly explained her condition and was told she could be seen as an NHS patient.

However, when she arrived, she was told she could not be treated under the NHS and would need to pay privately. As she is a single mother on benefits, she could not afford this at the time and was turned away without treatment, despite being in a serious condition.

She later had no choice but to return and pay privately to receive care.

In contrast, we attended another dental practice where they would not allow her to leave without receiving appropriate treatment, and showed genuine care and concern for her wellbeing.

Based on our experience, the communication and handling of her situation at Highbury Dental Care was extremely disappointing, especially given how unwell she was at the time. I transferred to So Energy in September 2025 and have been on the receiving end of a string of errors and appalling customer service from the outset.  Central to all of the problems is So Energy’s gross over estimation of my future gas usage.   In the year to September 2025, I used 18,591kWh of gas.  I am on track to use less than this in my first year with So Energy.  So Energy initially projected my gas usage figure for the year ahead as 68,494kW and, as at April 2026, is still projecting a figure of 48,555kwh per year, which is still more than two and a half times my actual usage rate.

This is not a consequence-free error. So Energy has used its projections to demand grossly inflated monthly direct debits payments, initially at a rate of approaching double what I should be paying (i.e. hundreds of pounds extra per month).  I have been hundreds of pounds in credit with So Energy throughout.  So Energy has never provided any explanation for its projected gas usage figures and when I have pointed out my actual usage figures, So Energy customer services just dismissed these as “not relevant” and stated that it operates in line with “industry norms”.  (I have had it confirmed that the actual Ofgem estimated norm for a property such as mine is 17,000kWh of gas usage per year)  So Energy’s approach just feels like a scam designed to grossly inflate the amount of customer credit it is holding.

I have repeatedly complained to So Energy about matters but it couldn't be bothered to properly review my complaints and said I could take matters to the Energy Ombudsman instead, presumably thinking I wouldn't bother. Unbelievably though, even having conceded all points to the Energy Ombudsman, So Energy is still attempting to unjustifiably increase my monthly payments, it still hasn't sorted out the grossly inflated gas projection figure and still hasn’t provided any explanation for how it arrives at its projections.  In addition, someone in So Energy has now apparently decided that the clever thing to do is to just ignore my emails on these recurrent and unresolved issues.  In addition to breaching its own complaint procedures, as well as those of Ofgem, this is really stupid because I am, and always have been, open to an amicable resolution of what are self-evident errors.

Summary: So Energy -- Awful experience over 7 months. So Energy owe us money and an account correction. Don't recommend.

ERROR ONE: Compromised meter readings & data.

Avoid This Dealership Unless You Want an 8-Month Legal Battle Over a Faulty Car
​If you are a car lover, please read this warning before stepping foot onto this forecourt. This dealership appears to hunt for highly desirable, rare specification vehicles to bait enthusiasts into buying cars that suffer from severe, inherent defects.
​I bought a beautifully specified L461 Range Rover Sport in a very rare Blue on Tan combination. Unfortunately, the stunning specification was a mask for a vehicle that was completely unfit for purpose and plagued by catastrophic water ingress. For months, this vehicle suffered from an ongoing water ingress defect where water continually flooded the rear boot lining and cabin floorboards, destroying the interior and threatening the complex electrical systems.
​The vehicle quality was entirely matched by the appalling, lazy, and utterly unprofessional customer service provided by the staff:
​Ryan & Dan: Unbelievably incompetent, took 30 minutes between several chats to his director for price negotiation, i almost walked out, and should have.
​Tom (Director): When these severe water ingress concerns were raised, Tom chose to entirely bury his head in the sand. His attitude was effectively to tell me "good luck" with a bad car, trying to call my bluff by forcing me to fight through my financial institution to get any semblance of justice.
The Delusion of Grandeur:
During a phone conversation, Tom personally told me that he aims for this dealership to be in the same league as prestigious, highly respected independent specialists like Alexanders Prestige and Redline Specialist Cars. If you want a laugh, go read the reviews for those long-established businesses, then look at how this company’s reviews are plummeting. True specialists protect their reputation at all costs and treat car lovers with respect. By dragging down the standards of the independent specialist market with lazy, predatory business practices, Tom and his team are giving genuine luxury dealers a bad name. They are not even in the same stratosphere as the reputable brands they claim to emulate.
​The 8-Month Battle and the Financial Verdict:
They thought I would roll over and accept a flooded luxury vehicle. They were wrong. I initiated a formal dispute through the finance provider, Black Horse.
​Following a 8-month ordeal, Black Horse officially sided with me. The bank’s explicit conclusion was that this supplying dealership provided a vehicle that was not of satisfactory quality and completely unfit for its purpose, and dangerous for use. Black Horse ordered a full buyback of the vehicle, forcing this dealership to take action for the defective car and refund my hard-earned money.
​Tom and his team should be utterly ashamed of how they treat consumers who spend vast amounts of money at their establishment. They count on you loving the car's spec so much that you will still trust them. Do not fall into their trap.
​I won my case, the bank exposed their practices, and they were legally forced to buy the vehicle back—but no consumer should have to endure an 8-month battle just to get a legal remedy. Buy from anyone else.

one_star_reviews.text:
My grandad recently stayed here for respite care while my nan was in hospital, and sadly every fear I had about this place became a reality.

Firstly, the room my grandad was placed in was shockingly small — I’ve genuinely stayed in hotel rooms bigger, cleaner, and far more comfortable than this. For somewhere that is supposed to provide care, comfort, and dignity, it felt incredibly disappointing.

My grandad has dementia, which already makes unfamiliar environments distressing, but it was made even worse by the fact that other residents were apparently allowed to walk freely into his room, go through his drawers, and torment him. It got to the point where my grandad was sitting in his chair with his walking stick between his legs because he felt he needed it to “fight off” the other residents who were frightening him. No elderly person should ever feel unsafe in a place they are supposed to be cared for.

He is also hard of hearing, and almost every day we visited, his hearing aid had “gone missing.” We repeatedly found it sitting at reception instead of being returned to him, leaving him unable to hear properly and causing him unnecessary distress and confusion.

One of the most heartbreaking visits was when he kept asking if we had come in the car because he wanted to get in and go home. He repeatedly told us, “the staff don’t do anything for me here.” Hearing that from someone you love is devastating.

We also have video evidence of my grandad in clear distress while staying here, begging to come home and showing how unhappy and uncomfortable he was. However, unlike others, I would never post videos or images showing my grandad’s face publicly in a review because I believe in protecting his identity, dignity, and privacy. His wellbeing should always come before proving a point online.

Thankfully, my grandad has now been moved elsewhere where he will be far more comfortable and properly cared for.

I had actually written a negative review when he first entered this care home because of the way the manager spoke down to me over the phone, along with what felt like a clear conflict of interest. I was asked to remove that review, and I did, purely because I didn’t want it to affect my grandad’s care. Sadly, it’s become very clear that it made no difference anyway.

I also feel it is important to mention that some of the positive reviews posted about this care home are not a true reflection of my grandad’s actual experience. Certain people leaving glowing reviews did not visit my grandad, were not involved in his care, and are only posting positively because the manager is a friend of a family member. That, in itself, shows a serious conflict of interest and makes those reviews feel misleading for families genuinely trying to choose safe and compassionate care for their loved ones.

I would not recommend this place to anyone looking for proper, dignified, and compassionate care for a family member.

My Dad had a 1week stay with no choice in the matter, the care he received was very poor.  He became very scared & distressed as other residents would just walk in his room, he also had items of property go missing.  One day when visiting in the evening we noticed his water jug was empty and the sticker on the jug showed it had been filled the day before, so no fresh water for 24 hours!! The photo below show the cloth I used to wipe the top of his drawers !! Dad went in with a few clothes so that wasn’t from !!

My father in law was unfortunate to spend 7 nights in this building. during his dementia restbite. I cant even call it a care home,due to the lack of care we experienced during our visits. Staff were non existent when needed, we would spend upto 2 hours per visit in his room with the door closed,no members of staff ever checked his wellbeing. Other residents were able to enter his room unchallenged, disturbing him during rest periods. He was frightened and anxious,this was not the care he needed.

I would not recommend this care home under any circumstances based on my grandad’s experience during his respite stay.
From the beginning, there appeared to be a clear lack of person-centred care and communication. My grandad has dementia and became extremely distressed during his stay. Despite being used to seeing family daily and regularly going out with us, I was told I could not take him out, even after this had reportedly been agreed with the social worker. This caused significant confusion and upset for him.

My grandad was frequently isolated in his room and rarely encouraged to spend time in communal areas. Most times I visited, he was alone in silence with no meaningful interaction from staff. Meals were often brought to his room where he ate alone, and other residents repeatedly entered his room, which frightened and distressed him to the point he began locking his own door.

There were continual issues with missing personal belongings and clothing. Items would regularly “reappear” late at night after concerns were raised. I also raised concerns regarding his hearing aid going missing, only to be told my grandad had lost it himself, despite him being unable to independently remove or insert it due to his condition.
I personally had to shave my grandad on occasions, and he informed me he had not been showered. I also pressed the buzzer for assistance on his behalf one day, only for a carer to open the door, say “okay,” and walk away without providing support once I communicated what he needed support with, leaving me to carry this out myself.

Basic care standards also appeared inconsistent. Fresh water was rarely replaced, and the jug was often too heavy for him to safely pour himself a drink. On one occasion, a carer asked if he had already had a cup of tea, accepted his confused response without checking, and walked away. This raises serious concerns around how fluid intake and wellbeing are monitored for vulnerable residents with dementia.

Communication between staff was also contradictory. I was initially told my grandad had a “great night with no concerns,” only to later be informed by management that he had actually had a restless night. Concerns frequently felt passed from “morning staff” to “night staff” without resolution.

I was also told by management that my grandad had been given corned beef pie and then a curry shortly afterwards. I fail to understand why two full meals would be provided one after another to a confused dementia patient.

There were further issues with staff awareness and honesty. On one occasion I was told my grandad was in the dining room, despite me explaining he had become too frightened to leave his room. I was spoken to dismissively, only to then find him exactly where I said he would be.. alone in his bedroom!!

Even simple concerns were ignored. My grandad had a television in his room with no remote control for a prolonged period, despite this being raised multiple times. Every visit, I would find him sat alone in silence until I manually turned the television on for him.
I have video evidence of my grandad expressing in his own words that he was unhappy and frightened during his stay. However, unlike others, I will not publicly share vulnerable footage of my grandad online.

I am grateful the appropriate authorities have been made aware of the concerns surrounding his stay. Families place enormous trust in care homes to protect vulnerable loved ones with dignity, compassion, and proper care. Unfortunately, based on our experience, I do not feel that happened here.

Subject: Feedback on Services and Payment Confirmation

Dear Esther and James,
We have forwarded payment as agreed in our contract. However, we feel it is important to share our concerns regarding the service we received.

We are extremely disappointed that, after spending nearly £X,000, we have nothing of real value or use to show for our time working with you. one_star_reviews.text:
Over the time our child attended this nursery, we unfortunately had a number of concerning experiences that ultimately led us to lose confidence in the care being provided.

One of the most worrying incidents for us involved our child being given a food we had specifically asked the nursery to avoid due to a previous reaction. There were also occasions where when looking on the daily diary on the famly app, our child had not been changed for almost 5 hours and when this was bought to the nurseries attention, the reason given to us for this happening was due to the lack of communication between staff. We also experienced limited communication at pick-up times regarding our child’s day and development.
We also raised a safeguarding concern during our time there which, from our perspective, was not handled with the level of urgency or reassurance we would have expected. This was something we felt needed to be escalated further at the time and took it upon ourselves to contact Ofsted. These examples contributed to our overall concerns. When visiting the nurseries Ofsted page you can see there has been 2 ‘concerns - actions taken’ one in 2022 and one in 2025 which we feel like parents should know.

The nursery environment often felt busy to us, and at times we felt the space appeared crowded. In our experience, this sometimes made the setting feel less calm than we would have hoped. On occasion at pick-up, it appeared to us that some staff were not actively engaging with the children but sat talking amongst themselves.
The outdoor areas, particularly for the under-2s, felt limited in terms of space and equipment. During our initial visit, trips and outings were mentioned; however, in our experience, these did not happen frequently during the time our child attended.
We also had some concerns about general upkeep. For example, during winter we noticed bin bags stored next to the bins at the gates of the outdoor play area, which we personally did not expect in a childcare environment. We are aware the nursery’s food hygiene rating has changed, which may be something prospective parents wish to look into for themselves.

A large part of our dissatisfaction relates to communication and management. During the initial show-round, we found the manager to be warm and reassuring. However, once our child started, our experience of communication was more limited. At times we felt our questions or requests were not fully addressed, and when we raised concerns, we did not always feel listened to or reassured. This left us feeling uncomfortable raising further issues as we were made to feel like we were the problem.

That said, we did have positive experiences with the Deputy Manager Becky and the admin Kelly, who we found to be helpful and approachable when we needed support.

It’s disappointing to write this review, as we understand the nursery previously had a strong reputation. However, based on our experience, we felt that standards of communication and overall care did not meet our expectations. We hope this feedback is taken constructively, as every child deserves a safe, attentive and well-managed environment.

*EDIT* After reading the ‘response’ aimed at anybody reading and not ourselves we would like to clarify,

Our child remained in this nurseries care for 4 sessions after my partner had left. This is because as full time working parents with bills to pay we had no other options but to leave her there. On the 4th session we withdrew our child immediately due to her nappy not being changed after 4 hours and 55 minutes despite us telling the room leader they were sore upon arrival to nursery that morning. As expected, they were left even more sore than they were before. This was put down to lack of communication between the room leader and her staff which simply isn’t good enough. We left work immediately to fetch our child.

I’ve been visiting this Subway location for a couple of years, and unfortunately the experience has been consistently poor.

The biggest issue is the management. On my second visit, I witnessed the franchise owner verbally abusing staff in front of customers, using insulting and condescending language such as asking if they were “stupid.” This wasn’t a one-off incident—I’ve since seen similar behaviour multiple times. It creates an uncomfortable atmosphere and is completely unacceptable in any workplace, especially in front of customers.

Customer service is also lacking. On one occasion, a customer raised a complaint and instead of trying to resolve it, the response was defensive—blaming how busy the store was and telling the customer they could return the food for a refund if they didn’t like it. That’s not how you build customer loyalty.

Over time, things have only gotten worse. The drinks fridge is often empty, cookies are frequently unavailable, and there’s limited choice of bread, sometimes not even fresh. This suggests deeper operational issues beyond just being busy.

The only positive I’ve seen was a newer staff member who showed great attitude, professionalism, and strong customer service skills. Unfortunately, that level of effort doesn’t seem to be reflected in the leadership.

I understand running a business is stressful, but repeatedly shouting at staff, threatening to deduct wages for mistakes, and handling customers poorly is not acceptable. It’s disappointing that after more than two years, nothing has improved.

I don’t believe the negative reviews for this place are unfair. Based on my experiences, these reviews reflect real and ongoing problems. I hope changes are made and that Subway recognises how poorly this franchise reflects on the company’s values and integrity, and takes appropriate action—for the sake of both staff and customers.

Subject: Concern Regarding Baby Weighing Facilities at Ashfield North East Children’s Centre

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to raise a concern regarding the baby weighing facilities at the Ashfield North East Children's Centre.

During my recent visit, I found the weighing station to be positioned in an extremely exposed area within the main reception. Its placement directly adjacent to public walkways and visible from the main entrance offers little to no privacy for parents and their babies. This is particularly concerning when changing nappies, as it requires parents to do so in full view of other visitors entering and passing through the reception area.

This environment does not feel parent- or baby-friendly and may cause discomfort or distress, especially for new parents. Basic privacy and dignity should be afforded when attending such essential services.

In contrast, the facilities at Mansfield Woodhouse Family Hub provide a far more appropriate setup. Their baby weighing station is located in a private room, away from public view, allowing parents to care for their babies without unnecessary exposure. I would strongly encourage your centre to consider a similar arrangement.

Furthermore, I was concerned to find that there was no wash basin or sink available nearby to wash hands after changing a dirty nappy. This raises significant hygiene concerns for both parents and babies. In comparison, the Mansfield Woodhouse Family Hub provides a wash basin with clean running water, enabling proper hand hygiene following nappy changes—something I would expect as a basic standard in such facilities.

Additionally, I noted that the weighing scale appears to be placed on a soft, cushioned surface rather than a firm, stable base. This raises concerns about the accuracy of the measurements and may mislead parents who rely on these readings to monitor their baby’s growth.

I would appreciate it if you could review the current setup and consider improvements to ensure the facility is safe, hygienic, accurate, and respectful of users’ privacy.

one_star_reviews.text:
NEGLIGENT, DISHONEST AND UNPROFESSIONAL BEYOND BELIEF – DO NOT RISK IT

We booked a home birth with Amie through Private Midwives and the ‘care’ I received from her was so awful in so many ways that I don’t know where to begin. My baby was born by emergency caesarean due to an undiagnosed breech which was not discovered until the 2nd stage of labour.

Amie failed to suspect the breech during 3 antenatal appointments, where she recorded the baby as head down. I should have been sent for a scan to check the presentation, but I wasn’t. But what is much worse, and what we only learnt later, is that Amie and her colleague should have been performing abdominal palpations during my labour to check the position of the baby. They did not do this even once. So not only did these midwives miss that the baby was breech – they were not even looking! Instead, they falsified these readings in the notes.

AMIE ALSO DISAPPEARED FROM MY HOMEBIRTH FOR 3 HOURS, just 1 hour after she had arrived. Not a word was said by either midwife about where she had gone or why. We later found out that AMIE HAD TAKEN HERSELF UPSTAIRS AND SLEPT IN OUR BED, WITHOUT OUR PERMISSION.

Amie and her colleague also ORDERED A MCDONALD’S TAKEAWAY TO OUR HOME DURING THE SECOND STAGE OF LABOUR. They knew I was feeling sick and that this was a major fear I had about birth, and they knew that I am vegan - but they ordered it anyway at 10:30 in the morning. They have since lied and said I gave them permission to do this. I did not.

The McDonald’s takeaway arrived during an obstetric emergency, just moments after the breech had been discovered. It was recommended I transfer to hospital for an emergency caesarean and me and my husband were told to go upstairs and decide what we wanted to do. This was despite the fact I had been downstairs for my entire labour. An emergency caesarean was my worst nightmare as I have a severe needle phobia, something which was discussed at length antenatally with Amie. Despite this, neither Amie or her colleague offered a single word of reassurance at this point. Neither Amie or her colleague gave us any information to enable us to make an informed decision. Me and my husband were then left upstairs scared and alone for 45 minutes whilst Amie and her colleague ate McDonald’s downstairs. They have since lied and said they came upstairs but did not want to disturb me as I was very upset. Not true – we left the bathroom door wide open. We did not want to be alone. They could not have come upstairs without our knowing it.

Despite neither Amie or her colleague caring for me during this time, there was a 17-MINUTE DELAY IN RINGING THE AMBULANCE. Amie and her colleague also tried to blame this on me and my husband, by saying that we told her not to ring one – another lie.

The baby’s heartrate was also not monitored properly in my labour. During the 2nd stage it should have been listened to at least once every 5 minutes (as per NICE guidelines). Amie and her colleague listened in on average just once every 29 minutes during my confirmed second stage. So, they should have been monitoring the heartrate 6 times as often as they were.

Even once the breech was discovered and they were dealing with an obstetric emergency, they did not monitor me or the baby properly. During this time, they left us completely unattended whilst they ate McDonald’s takeaway. My heartrate was also not monitored properly during labour. They did not check my blood pressure even once. They did not check my temperature even once. Instead, they falsified all of these readings. These are just some of the issues with the ‘care’ I received and some of the lies Amie has told since the birth. There are so many more that it would be impossible to fit them all into the space available for this review. We have reported Amie to the Nursing and Midwifery Council, who are currently investigating her fitness to practice as a midwife.

We visited a property through Tanners Properties Nottingham, and unfortunately the experience was disappointing from start to finish.

The agent arrived late, and multiple groups were allowed to view the property at the same time. It felt more like an auction than a proper viewing, with no structure or consideration for individual applicants.

The agent made little effort to engage—there was no proper introduction, no guidance during the viewing, and he simply stood aside while people walked around. At the end, he briefly mentioned the application process, which involves completing forms that go very deep into personal details. I understand background checks are necessary, but the level of information requested felt excessive and intrusive.

It’s also surprising that a company operating this way doesn’t manage proper appointment slots or a more professional system. Background checks could easily be handled through established services like Experian or ClearScore, rather than putting all the burden on applicants. It gave the impression they are trying to cut costs at the expense of customer experience.

Although the property itself was good, the service was poor enough that we decided not to proceed.

Based on this experience, I would not recommend them.
